reasons: Section 22.1 as drafted (audit 'at any time without notice' plus remote access to Customer systems) is squarely in walk-away territory on frequency, notice and system access, so a deviation finding is correct and the clause does not meet the fallback.

The redline reaches the preferred position with the correct parameters (once per twelve months, 30 days' prior written notice, business hours, independent auditor under written confidentiality, off-site where practicable) and deletes the remote/direct system-access language as the redline guidance requires.

The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic (0.825 changed-character ratio) is acceptable here: the original sentence contains no usable limits, so a full rewrite is the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position; the cost-allocation and access-carve-out sentences in 22.2 are correctly left untouched and are not double-flagged.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, explains the change, notes the resolved conflict with 22.2, and offers the 15-day fallback while holding the line on system access. The rationale's passing reference to a Section 22.3 not included in the supplied excerpts is immaterial to the edit.
